patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Genesys and respond.io share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Genesys only if your buying job matches “Enterprise CCaaS (Genesys Cloud CX) — CX 1 from $75/user/mo annual; CX 2 $115; CX 3 $155; ” rather than respond.io's shape. Choose respond.io only if your buying job matches “Omnichannel customer messaging platform (WhatsApp + other channels) with shared inbox and ” rather than Genesys's shape. Workflow advantage: Genesys leans contact-center, sales-calling; respond.io leans whatsapp-support. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Genesys and respond.io share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Genesys is Enterprise CCaaS (Genesys Cloud CX) — CX 1 from $75/user/mo annual; CX 2 $115; CX 3 $155; CX 4 $240.; respond.io is Omnichannel customer messaging platform (WhatsApp + other channels) with shared inbox and AI — Starter from $79/month annual-equivalent..
- Company-size focus: Genesys (mid-market, enterprise) vs respond.io (small-business, mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Genesys-leaning contact-center, sales-calling vs respond.io-leaning whatsapp-support.
- Researched limits: Genesys — Enterprise complexity and implementation cost — not an SMB self-serve phone; respond.io — Not a business phone system — no IVR, queues or PSTN calling product.

Limitations — Genesys: Enterprise complexity and implementation cost — not an SMB self-serve phone; CX 1 is voice-only; digital channels require CX 2 or digital add-ons; respond.io: Not a business phone system — no IVR, queues or PSTN calling product; Platform subscription plus channel/Meta messaging fees create two-layer TCO.

Poor-fit cases: Genesys is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Enterprise complexity and implementation cost — not an SMB self-serve phone · respond.io is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a business phone system — no IVR, queues or PSTN calling product · Avoid Genesys if you actually need respond.io's motion (Omnichannel customer messaging platform (WhatsApp + other channels) with shared )

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
